title: DeepSeek prices web search and page fetch at $0.75 per thousand calls
friendlyTitle: DeepSeek charges 75 cents for a thousand web searches
summary: DeepSeek's Search and Fetch APIs are now documented as raw JSON tools for agents and retrieval apps, backed by the company's own search engine. Search returns structured results; Fetch returns one page as Markdown. Each successful request costs $0.75 per thousand calls, not per token or per result. Empty searches, failures, and timeouts are not billed. Calls made through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, or Codex stay free until 00:00 Beijing time on 1 November 2026.
friendlySummary: DeepSeek now sells two tools for agents. One searches the web. The other fetches a page and returns it as text. A successful call costs $0.75 per thousand requests. You do not pay for failed calls, empty searches, or timeouts. If the call comes through DeepSeek Harness, Claude Code, or Codex, it stays free until 1 November 2026, Beijing time.
whyItMatters: If an agent searches the web on your account, the new line item is the request, not the model tokens. The account limit is 5 requests a second for each API, and Fetch can still fail when a site blocks it.
friendlyWhyItMatters: If an agent searches the web on your account, you pay for the search itself, not only for the model's words. Each account is limited to five searches a second, and some sites will still refuse the page fetch.
